Parse the output of a TreePPL SMC run

Source: R/post-process.R
tp_parse_smc.Rd

tp_parse_smc() reads the JSON output of a TreePPL run with a sequential Monte Carlo method (e.g. "smc-bpf", "smc-apf") and returns the samples, their weights and the normalising constant of each sweep as a tibble.

Usage

tp_parse_smc(json_path, wide = TRUE)

Arguments

json_path

Path(s) to one or more JSON output files, as returned by tp_run(). Sweeps are numbered consecutively across files.

wide

Logical. If TRUE (default), one row per particle and one column per parameter. If FALSE, one row per particle and parameter, with columns parameter and sample.

Value

A tibble with columns:

  • sweep: sweep number.

  • particle: particle number within its sweep.

  • log_weight: the particle's log weight.

  • norm_constant: the sweep's log normalising constant.

  • norm_weight: the normalised weight (see Details).

  • one column per parameter (wide = TRUE), or parameter and sample (wide = FALSE).

Details

Each line of an SMC output file is one sweep, with the particles' samples, their log weights and the sweep's log normalising constant (normConst). TreePPL writes NaN and infinite values as {"__float__": "-inf"}; these are read as R's NaN, Inf and -Inf.

Sweeps are skipped when they have no samples (every particle had zero weight) or a normalising constant that is NaN or -Inf; a message reports how many. Particles with a non-finite log weight are dropped. If no sweep has usable samples, the function stops with an error: try more particles, or check the input data and priors.

The normalised weight of a particle is exp(log_weight + norm_constant - max(log_weight + norm_constant)), taken over all particles of all sweeps, so the heaviest particle gets weight 1.

Parameters are named after the fields of the model's return type when the output has them (e.g. lambda, mu), and x1, x2, ... otherwise. Non-scalar values (vectors, trees) are kept as list-columns.

See also

tp_run(), which calls this function for SMC runs, and tp_parse_mcmc() for MCMC output.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
sampler <- tp_sampler(model = "crbd", method = "smc-bpf")
data <- tp_data(model = "crbd", dataList = list(tree = tree, rho = 0.5))
run <- tp_run(sampler, data, particles = 1000, sweeps = 10)

# Parse an output file directly
samples <- tp_parse_smc("out.json")
samples_long <- tp_parse_smc("out.json", wide = FALSE)
} # }
